# TDPdf v1.24.1.0

**Text boxes work.** Insert a text box, and it stays there long enough to type in. That has not reliably been true since 1.23.2.0, and five releases were spent on the wrong explanation.

## What was actually wrong

Placing a text box opens a live editor on the page. Something else in the app was walking up to that editor and settling it — turning it into a finished (and therefore empty, and therefore discarded) annotation — a few dozen milliseconds after it appeared. From the outside that looks exactly like "Insert Text Box does nothing."

Four releases chased it as a focus problem. It was not. The telemetry added in 1.24.0.0 recorded which method asked for the commit, and the first report back named it on every single occurrence: the zoom. **54 of 54 editor destructions across the fleet came from `ApplyZoom`** — which repeats, roughly 23 times a second, for as long as the editor is alive. The 400 ms protective window added in 1.23.7.0 did not stop that; it just moved every death to between 409 and 456 ms, and the next pass took the editor anyway.

The zoom never needed to do this. The page image and both annotation layers are all sized from one fixed render box, and zoom is applied as a transform on their common parent, so a live box's position — and the annotation it eventually becomes — is the same number at every zoom level. There was nothing to settle. The call is gone.

For the record, because it cost four releases: the two focus-related events in the telemetry have fired **zero** times in the product's history, and placement has reported the editor attached and focused every single time. The editor was being destroyed *while focused*. The one successful text annotation ever recorded in the fleet came from a user who managed a keystroke within 29 ms and won the race.

## Two zoom bugs went with it

- **The zoom dropdown was reading its own updates back as your input.** Every zoom the app computed — a window resize, a fit, opening a document — updated the dropdown, and that update came back in as though a person had picked it. The app then cancelled whatever fit mode you had chosen and applied a zoom nobody asked for.
- **A computed fit was being snapped to the nearest preset.** Fit Width or Fit Page landing anywhere near 100% was quietly forced to exactly 100%, changing the fit you asked for.

Both are fixed. If Fit Width has been drifting off on you, or the zoom box has seemed to have a mind of its own, that was this.

## What this changes for administrators

**The Intune detection rule now requires 1.24.1.0, so managed machines pick this up on the next evaluation. Assignments are unaffected.** Nothing about telemetry configuration changes — `OtlpEndpoint` and `OtlpToken` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\TDPdf\Telemetry` are exactly as they were.

One new event, `Zoom.Churn`, is added to the telemetry and disclosed in `PRIVACY.md` — as is `Annotation.TextEditorCommitDeferred`, which shipped in 1.23.7.0 and was left out of the privacy policy at the time. The repeated zoom passes described above were only ever visible because a text editor happened to be alive while they ran, and that signal disappears now that the editor survives. So the viewport reports the repetition directly: if it re-applies its zoom 8 or more times a second and keeps doing so for at least two seconds, it says how many, for how long, and names the method in TDPdf's own source that originated them. The sustain requirement matters: a sidebar animation and a window-edge drag both exceed that rate by design, and neither is a fault. Those names are fixed when the program is compiled — the event cannot reference a document, a page, or anything typed — and it is rate-limited to one report every 15 minutes. The repetition itself is a real defect and is tracked separately in [#132](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/issues/132); this release stops it from destroying your work while that is dealt with properly.
